title: Pending electronic cancellation versus already collected split-cash reporting
scope: Bounded state-transition and accounting-projection comparison: domain cancellation, server persistence, payment-channel query, and existing split/cancellation test coverage. Corroborates existing FIN-002; no duplicate finding or runtime incidence claim.

behavior.before_cancel: For a Multi order with cash and pending electronic legs, PaymentMethodTotals counts the cash leg immediately and skips the pending electronic leg, as documented and tested.
behavior.cancel_transition: CancelElectronicPayment marks the entire order Cancelled, IsPaid false and ElectronicPayment Cancelled. The handler persists those fields and audit event but does not post a reversing treasury movement.
behavior.after_cancel_projection: Both PaymentMethodTotals and CashRefundsFromOrders skip orders with Cancelled status before processing payment splits/refunds. Consequently, after cancelling an order that already contributed an immediate cash split leg, the reporting projection drops that cash amount while this cancellation path does not reverse it. This supports FIN-002’s source-level accounting discrepancy; whether a mixed payment can complete this precise lifecycle operationally and how the owner intends partial cancellation remain policy/flow validation questions.

cross_file_call_chain: Checkout creates a Multi split order and immediate cash movement -> CancelPendingElectronicPaymentHandler.HandleAsync -> Order.CancelElectronicPayment -> persists Status=cancelled and payment status -> OrderPaymentQueries.PaymentMethodTotals/CashRefundsFromOrders skip cancelled order -> SalesRules and ShiftReconciliation use those query results.
counterevidence_and_limits: The linked split test establishes that immediate cash is counted while a sibling electronic leg is pending, but does not cancel the order.
Cancellation tests cover only a pure electronic order; no regression test combines a split cash leg with cancellation.
The handler writes an audit event and correctly does not reverse a nonexistent electronic movement; it also does not reverse the already-posted cash leg.
FIN-001 records a separate electronic confirmation path gap. This comparison does not prove a live mixed order was cancelled or cash was lost.
No database/runtime behavior was executed; reports here are projections of source query rules.
future_action: Implement the already identified FIN-002 fix only after deciding the business invariant: either partial cancellation preserves the fulfilled cash sale and leaves the order financially active for collected legs, or whole-order cancellation creates an explicit, authorized compensating cash movement/refund and reconciles inventory/order state. Do not simply exclude the cancelled order from totals while retaining its cash movement. Preserve audit trail and idempotent request semantics.

tests.existing_test_evidence: Pure split pending cash accounting is tested; pure electronic cancellation is tested; mixed cancellation is not.
needed: Domain/integration test: create 100 cash + 100 pending InstaPay, confirm cash movement once, cancel electronic leg, then assert order state, cash channel, drawer expectation and treasury movement follow owner-approved invariant.
Retry same cancellation key and assert no duplicate compensating movement or audit event beyond intended replay semantics.
Test full immediate split and pure-electronic cancellation controls.

source_references.evidence: Cancellation changes whole Order.Status to Cancelled, IsPaid false and electronic status to Cancelled; no treasury reversal is performed by the aggregate.
Handler persists cancelled order/electronic status and audit event under an order-row transaction; it has no treasury movement reversal.

Both payment-channel and cash-refund projections skip any OrderStatus.Cancelled before processing payment splits/refunds. For active multi orders, cash split legs count immediately while electronic legs await confirmation.
A split cash+InstaPay order counts the cash leg and excludes pending electronic before cancellation; it does not assert post-cancel reporting.
Cancellation tests use a pure InstaPay order, confirming whole-order Cancelled status but not the mixed split cash consequence.

limitations: The intended accounting treatment of canceling one pending leg when another leg is already collected requires owner/business-policy confirmation.
No claim of runtime transaction loss or live user impact.
